title: How a tunnel under the sea is built

lines.en: You need to get cars across the sea. But giant ships pass through here every day, so a bridge is out.
So you start digging a tunnel from the beach, straight under the water.
And the sea says: thank you very much, and pours right in.
So this time, you don't dig under the sea. You dig on the bottom of it. A dredger scoops out a long trench across the seabed.
Then you spread a perfectly flat bed of gravel along the bottom of the trench.
Meanwhile, on the shore, you build a giant dry pit next to the sea.
Inside it, you cast huge hollow boxes of concrete. These are the pieces of your tunnel.
You seal both ends of every piece with steel walls, so not a single drop gets in.
Now you flood the dock. And the concrete box... floats! It's full of air, so it behaves like a ship.
Tugboats drag it out to sea, right above the trench.
You fill tanks inside it with water, and it slowly sinks, down onto the gravel bed.
Each piece has a fat rubber seal on its end. You pull it tight against the last piece.
Then you pump out the water trapped between them. And now the whole sea pushes on the other end, squeezing the joint shut. Free pressure!
Piece after piece, the tunnel crosses the whole strait.
You bury it under tons of rock, so anchors and currents can never touch it.
Knock out the steel walls, pave the road, turn on the lights. Congratulations! You have built a tunnel under the sea.
